content.body:
As the Bf 109 series became increasingly depended on by the Luftwaffe as its primary day fighter, the strain on production of its Daimler Benz DB.601 engine became untenable. The Fw 190A was designed to be the Bf 109's stable-mate and rely on a radial engine from BMW, the BMW801.
With a stout and compact airframe being pulled along by a 1700+ hp BMW engine, the Focke Wulf 190 boasted speed, acceleration and climb rate that were better than its main rival, the Spitfire Mk V and, While the classic turn radius or turn rate had long been the focus of air combat maneuvering in the past, the Fw 190 changed all that with its tremendous roll rate. While not able to out turn most of its enemies, the Fw 190 could roll faster and thereby change its maneuver vector (its turning direction) faster. The Fw 190 is a difficult plane to master as it relies on a performance profile that is vastly different from most other fighters in the game. Speed, acceleration and roll rate are the assets of the Butcherbird that make this difference. But pilots coming from the Bf 109 series must re-calibrate their minds in order to unlock the Fw 190's power.
Out roll your opponent to turn a defensive position into an offensive one, particularly useful are the barrel roll suite of maneuvers. The Butcherbird retains its speed very well in this type of rolling fight and can easily disengage at will if flown with a cool head and a soft touch. Once you get someone in your sights, the four 20 mm cannons make it very short work to knock down any aircraft, allowing you to quickly change targets.
The Fw 190 was also often referred to as the "Würger" ("Slayer").
